text:
raj.kapoor: AcmeHealth just pinged support — they saw bulk object downloads from their Dedicated tenant around 2026-03-18T22:14:30Z and suspect a data exfil. They provided a few object names and an external IP. Can we triage for egress + KMS misuse?

emma.ops: copying eng-infra and security. can you paste the exact timestamps and object keys they shared?

raj.kapoor: they sent: 2026-03-18T22:12:34Z - 2026-03-18T22:15:02Z. objects: /acme-prod/patient_exports/2026-03-18/export-1.csv, export-2.csv. external dst ip: 34.86.12.9 (customer says not a partner).

daniel.oncall: oncall here. starting with flow logs + audit logs query. running: 
```
# audit log query (internal)
select * from audit_logs
where resource.type="dedicated_tenant"
  and resource.labels.tenant_id="acme-prod"
  and proto_payload.methodName in ("v1.objects.get","v1.objects.list","v1.objects.getSignedUrl")
  and timestamp >= "2026-03-18T22:00:00Z"
  and timestamp <= "2026-03-18T22:30:00Z"
order by timestamp desc
```

sec-bot: ALERT: anomalous_bulk_download detected for tenant acme-prod — confidence 0.87. service_account: svc-acme-data-processor@acme-prod.iam. Last seen: 2026-03-18T22:14:59Z.

emma.ops: flow logs show outbound to 34.86.12.9 on port 443 from 10.8.45.12 (node hosting tenant). snippet: "2026-03-18T22:14:58Z src=10.8.45.12 dst=34.86.12.9 proto=TCP bytes=123456"

tina.cs: customer says those object keys are PHI exports and they did not authorize an external transfer. they're urgent and want containment steps now.

daniel.oncall: containment plan proposal: 1) disable svc-acme-data-processor service account tokens (block immediate access), 2) add temporary egress deny rule for tenant subnets to external IPs except approved partners, 3) take KMS key out of rotation path (deny Decrypt for the SA) to prevent further decrypts, 4) snapshot audit logs and S3/object metadata and hand to Sec for forensics.

raj.kapoor: FYI disabling SA tokens will break scheduled exports for legitimate jobs. need CS + customer signoff for full disable. we can do targeted revoke for the single key used if we identify it.

emma.ops: I can apply a targeted deny rule for that external IP now (quick, reversible). will also take a copy of object ACLs and object versions. doing IP block now: `fwctl deny-src 10.8.45.0/24 dst 34.86.12.9`

sec-bot: action logged: temporary firewall rule created by emma.ops at 1769954452.

daniel.oncall: audit query returned calls using KMS key kms-acme-prod-01 decrypt by svc-acme-data-processor at 22:14:57Z. attaching minimal tx id: tx_0a9c3. Looks like the SA called object GETs with valid signatures — implies SA had Decrypt on the key.

tina.cs: customer provided their internal admin didn’t run this. they want us to rotate key and provide timeline.

legal.team: preserve all logs, do not delete anything. label as potential customer data exposure. I'll join the incident call. Need a timeline and comms draft before we notify wider org or regulators.

raj.kapoor: agreed. next steps: (A) secure environment: emma applied IP block; daniel please revoke the specific service-account key or rotate creds for svc-acme-data-processor (not full SA disable unless customer approves). (B) sec team to run forensics on where the SA key was used from (IP, host) and whether credentials were exfiltrated. (C) escalate to PM/ops to check recent RBAC changes — did any recent policy grant Decrypt to that SA?

daniel.oncall: revoking the specific key now: `iam revoke-key svc-acme-data-processor key-id=key-7f2a` — done at 1769954620. confirm?

sec-bot: event: service_account_key_revoke by daniel.oncall at 1769954620.

emma.ops: starting retention-preserving export of audit logs and object metadata to internal forensic bucket. command: `audit-export --tenant acme-prod --range 22:00-22:30 --dest s3://forensics/acme-prod/176995`

raj.kapoor: good. daniel, please also collect the process/container metadata from node 10.8.45.12 and preserve image hashes.

daniel.oncall: collected container logs and mounted volumes snapshot uploaded to s3://forensics-acme-prod/176995/host-10-8-45-12.tar.gz at 1769954750.

tina.cs: customer wants a short-notes timeline and confirmation that we're investigating. can we send a customer-safe acknowledgement?

legal.team: draft ack: "We've detected anomalous activity in your Dedicated environment. We've taken temporary containment measures (blocked outbound to the observed IP, revoked the implicated service account key) and are preserving all logs for forensic review. We will provide a timeline and next steps within 24 hours." get customer approval before wording changes.

raj.kapoor: assigning follow-ups: sec forensics: @sec-team (daniel + emma) lead, action items: full timeline, root cause hypothesis, indicators of compromise (IOCs). cs: tina to coordinate customer comms. legal: hold on regulator-notify until we have confirmed exfil. eng-infra: raj to audit RBAC changes last 30 days.

emma.ops: quick note for post-incident: add RBAC baseline check to CI (deny any new Decrypt grants to non-admin SAs without 2-person review). also add an automated alert when a KMS key is used by a non-standard SA.

raj.kapoor: thanks everyone. creating incident ticket INC-2026-176995 and schedule 1hr deep-dive in 30m. will post the runbook and attach exported logs.

sec-bot: incident INC-2026-176995 created and assigned to sec-team at 1769954845.

emma.ops: will follow up in the incident ticket with raw queries and artifacts.

tina.cs: sending initial acknowledgement to customer now and scheduling a call. :phone:

daniel.oncall: will continue triage, will report back with initial forensics by +2h.

raj.kapoor: closing thread here for Slack — all official updates to be in INC-2026-176995. thanks.
